name: rust-studio
description: Rust engineering workflows through 11 outcome skills and five execution roles with reusable domain profiles. Fresh design review, implementation handoff, independent acceptance, path-scoped standards and cargo-aware hooks for libraries, async services, CLIs and systems code.

test_runner.title: Default test runner
test_runner.description: Test runner the studio prefers (cargo-nextest recommended). Surfaced in the session briefing so agents honor it.

gate_intensity.title: Default gate intensity
gate_intensity.description: How many independent lenses review a change: full (every relevant gate + the multi-lens pass), lean (one reviewer, the directly-relevant gate), or solo (a single advisory pass). This scales reviewers and cost only — the evidence bar never moves, and unsafe / public-API / release changes run full whatever this says. Because lean and solo remove the readers that would otherwise catch a gamed green, stop_guard defaults ON under them unless you set it explicitly.

default_msrv.title: House MSRV fallback
default_msrv.description: Minimum supported Rust version to assume when a Cargo.toml does not declare rust-version (e.g. 1.82). Leave empty to keep showing "(unset)".

memory_recall.title: Session-start memory recall
memory_recall.description: At session start, rank the project memory index against the branch / changed crates / last commit, surface relevant notes and report index health; on each prompt, point at matching notes once per session. Turn off to skip both. The host still loads its index; inspect-project recall, review-work memory and authorized write-docs memory/handoff modes remain available.

memory_dir.title: Project memory directory
memory_dir.description: Where project memory lives. Leave empty to use the host's auto-memory directory for this repository (Claude Code's autoMemoryDirectory setting, else ~/.claude/projects/<project-key>/memory) — the same MEMORY.md index Claude Code loads at session start, shared with Codex sessions. Set it only to keep the studio's memory somewhere else; Claude Code will not load that index itself, so the session-start hook carries it instead.

auto_capture.title: Auto-capture learnings
auto_capture.description: After a completed unit with no saved memory, nudge once to consider durable candidates for write-docs memory mode. The reminder grants no write authorization; host/user policy still governs capture. Never re-blocks the same turn. Turn off to disable this reminder.

acceptance_guard.title: Acceptance guard (block ending with unmet ledger gates)
acceptance_guard.description: For session-bound acceptance.md under docs/designs/<slug>/ or legacy .rust-studio/specs/<slug>/, block completion claims while gates are unmet, stale or malformed. Binding uses full artifact paths. Questions, plan-only handoffs and honest NEEDS WORK/BLOCKED are not completion claims. Parses state without executing CHECK; feedback supplies --reverify. Releases after four stops without progress and fails open. Custom locations require direct checking with --cwd <root>. Turn off to keep the ledger advisory.

statusline.title: Auto-install status line
statusline.description: On the first session, install the rich studio status line into ~/.claude/settings.json. Installed once, preserves an existing statusLine, and backs settings up first. Turn off to skip auto-install; explicitly invoke maintain-studio status-line mode to manage or remove it.

progress_tracking.title: Progress visibility
progress_tracking.description: When on, implement-change and other coordinating workflows mirror artifact-backed progress to the host task surface and report phase results. Durable tasks and execution evidence remain authoritative. Turn off to reduce progress narration.

git_guard.title: Irreversible-action guard
git_guard.description: Block Bash commands that destroy work with no way back (git reset --hard, clean -f, checkout ., branch -D, stash drop, force-push, reflog expire) or that publish permanently (a real cargo publish / cargo yank). Plain git push, --force-with-lease, and cargo publish --dry-run stay allowed. The studio decides tactical calls on its own, so this is the line where autonomy stops. Turn off to run unguarded.

routing_nudge.title: Routing nudge
routing_nudge.description: Once per session, remind you to prefer a Studio outcome skill and use inspect-project recall mode for relevant prior decisions. Turn off to silence the UserPromptSubmit nudge.

fmt_nudge.title: Formatting nudge
fmt_nudge.description: After a turn that changed .rs files, nudge to use verify-work lint mode when they are not rustfmt-clean. Turn off to silence the Stop-hook fmt check.

lifecycle_notes.title: Session-lifecycle notes
lifecycle_notes.description: Remind the session to preserve in-flight artifact/task evidence before compaction and use write-docs handoff mode at session end. Memory-store writes still require authorization. Turn off to silence both.

stop_guard.title: Stop-guard (block undisciplined turn endings)
stop_guard.description: Block the turn from ending if the final message dodges ownership, seeks permission, stops early, avoids tests, leaves stubs, hands the work back to you, or claims done without evidence. The feedback is fed back to the model so it continues — the mechanical teeth for docs/integrity-and-evidence.md. Defaults to OFF at gate_intensity full (the extra review lenses already catch this) and ON at lean/solo (they don't). Set it explicitly to override that coupling in either direction.

stop_guard_strict.title: Stop-guard: strict mode
stop_guard_strict.description: Also block on soft signals (speculation, weak completion, evidence-free claims) even when some completion evidence is present. Requires stop_guard on.

stop_guard_require_evidence.title: Stop-guard: require evidence
stop_guard_require_evidence.description: Block any turn ending whose final message lacks concrete completion evidence (files changed / commands run / verification / result), even with no flagged phrase. Requires stop_guard on.

stop_guard_allow_categories.title: Stop-guard: allowed categories
stop_guard_allow_categories.description: Comma-separated stop-guard categories to exempt from blocking (e.g. "speculation,fake-certainty"). Useful to tune false positives without turning the guard off. Requires stop_guard on.
